svg.title: Amazon Kinesis Data Streams
svg.desc: Amazon Kinesis Data Streams. Managed streaming: records go to shards by partition key, and consumers read each shard in order and can replay it. Step 1, Where it sits: Producers put clicks into the stream clicks; Lambda, Firehose and Flink each read every record. Step 2, Shards and partition keys: MD5 puts key s-41 in shard 1's hash key range; the record is stamped 842, after s-41's 837. Step 3, Two kinds of consumers: Lambda and Firehose poll and share each shard's 2 MB/s; Flink's enhanced fan-out gets its own. Step 4, Hot shards and limits: Bot session s-90 overloads shard 2 while the others have room: fix the key, split or go on-demand.

g.text: Producers put clicks into the stream clicks; Lambda, Firehose and Flink each read every record.
MD5 puts key s-41 in shard 1's hash key range; the record is stamped 842, after s-41's 837.
Lambda and Firehose poll and share each shard's 2 MB/s; Flink's enhanced fan-out gets its own.
Bot session s-90 overloads shard 2 while the others have room: fix the key, split or go on-demand.
one batch per shard at a time, in order
EFO: own 2 MB/s per shard, pushed
Web servers and the mobile API put about 2,000 clicks a second into 4 shards; AWS runs the servers and replicates across 3 AZs.
Reading doesn't remove a record: Lambda, Firehose and Flink each read all of them, and any of them can replay up to 7 days.
MD5 turns s-41 into a 128-bit hash key, 6e19676a… in hex: inside shard 1's range, so every click of session s-41 lands there.
The record gets sequence number 842, after s-41's 837. A shard takes 1 MB/s or 1,000 records/s in and gives 2 MB/s out.
Lambda and Firehose poll each shard with GetRecords and share its 2 MB/s; Flink's enhanced fan-out gets its own 2 MB/s, pushed.
Each reader keeps its own position: Lambda moves on only after a batch succeeds, and Firehose writes a file per 5 MiB or 300 s.
HOT SHARD: FIX THE KEY, SPLIT THE SHARD OR GO ON-DEMAND
Bot session s-90 adds 600 clicks/s to shard 2, which now needs 1,100/s: about 100/s are rejected while shards 0, 1 and 3 use half.
